# Render Commands

Header: `winui/render/Renderer.hpp`.

## struct FillRoundedRect

Recorded form of [Renderer::fill_rounded_rect()](renderer.md#fill_rounded_rect): a solid rounded-rect fill.

Example: 
```cpp
// What Renderer::fill_rounded_rect() draws. In an element of your own:
class Panel : public ui::Element
{
    void render_override(ui::Renderer& r, const ui::RenderContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Theme& theme = context.theme;
        r.fill_rounded_rect(bounds(), 4.0f, theme.colors().background);
    }
};
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bounds` | `Rect` |  | The rect to fill, in DIPs. |
| `radius` | `float` | `0.0f` | Corner radius in DIPs; 0 is a plain rect. |
| `color` | `Color` |  | The fill color. |

## struct FillRoundedRectGradient

A gradient fill of a rounded rect (radius 0 == a plain rect), along the brush's [GradientAxis](namespace-ui.md#gradientaxis): the XP/Vista counterpart to [FillRoundedRect](#struct-fillroundedrect)'s flat color. Recorded form of [Renderer::fill_rounded_rect_gradient()](renderer.md#fill_rounded_rect_gradient).

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bounds` | `Rect` |  | The rect to fill, in DIPs. |
| `radius` | `float` | `0.0f` | Corner radius in DIPs. |
| `brush` | `LinearGradientBrush` |  | Stops and axis, mapped across [`bounds`](#struct-fillroundedrectgradient). |

## struct FillEllipse

A filled ellipse, given by its center and radii. A circle (radius_x == radius_y) given this way has none of the rounding ambiguity of a square rect with a corner radius. The classic circular radio-button bevel is built from these.

Example: 
```cpp
renderer.fill_ellipse(ui::Point{10, 10}, 6, 6, ui::colors::White);
renderer.stroke_ellipse(ui::Point{10, 10}, 6, 6, ui::colors::Black, 1.0f);
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `center` | `Point` |  | Center, in DIPs. |
| `radius_x` | `float` | `0.0f` | Horizontal radius, in DIPs. |
| `radius_y` | `float` | `0.0f` | Vertical radius, in DIPs. |
| `color` | `Color` |  | The fill color. |

## struct FillPolygon

A straight-edged polygon filled with one color, such as a menu's cascade arrow. The shape is always closed; [StrokePolyline](#struct-strokepolyline) outlines one.

Example: 
```cpp
renderer.fill_polygon(ui::FillPolygon{
    .points = {{0, 10}, {8, 0}, {16, 10}},
    .fill   = ui::colors::White,
});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `points` | `std::vector<Point>` |  | Vertices in DIPs, in drawing order. |
| `fill` | `Color` |  | Interior color; transparent paints nothing. |

## struct FillRectPattern

Recorded form of [Renderer::fill_rect_pattern()](renderer.md#fill_rect_pattern): [`bounds`](#struct-fillrectpattern) filled with a [Pattern](namespace-ui.md#pattern) in two colors.

Example: 
```cpp
// The Windows 95 scrollbar trough.
const ui::Rect trough{0, 16, 16, 200};
renderer.fill_rect_pattern(trough, ui::Pattern::Checkerboard50, ui::colors::White,
                           ui::Color::from_rgba(192, 192, 192));
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bounds` | `Rect` |  | The rect to fill, in DIPs. |
| `pattern` | `Pattern` | `Pattern::Checkerboard50` | Which stipple. |
| `fg` | `Color` |  | The "on" pixels. |
| `bg` | `Color` |  | The "off" pixels. |

## struct StrokeRoundedRect

Recorded form of [Renderer::stroke_rounded_rect()](renderer.md#stroke_rounded_rect): a solid outline of a rounded rect, centered on [`bounds`](#struct-strokeroundedrect)' edge (so half of [`stroke_width`](#struct-strokeroundedrect) falls outside it).

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bounds` | `Rect` |  | The rect the stroke is centered on, in DIPs. |
| `radius` | `float` | `0.0f` | Corner radius in DIPs; 0 is a plain rect. |
| `color` | `Color` |  | The stroke color. |
| `stroke_width` | `float` | `1.0f` | Pen width in DIPs. |

## struct StrokeRoundedRectGradient

The stroke counterpart of [FillRoundedRectGradient](#struct-fillroundedrectgradient), used for Fluent's elevation border: a linear gradient stroked around a rounded rect. The gradient spans [`extent_px`](#struct-strokeroundedrectgradient) device pixels whatever the height of [`bounds`](#struct-strokeroundedrectgradient) (Fluent uses 3). A positive span starts at `bounds.top()` and [`brush`](#struct-strokeroundedrectgradient)'s stops read top to bottom. A negative span starts at `bounds.bottom()` and the stops read bottom to top, which is how an accent control's flipped border is drawn.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bounds` | `Rect` |  | The rect the stroke is centered on, in DIPs. |
| `radius` | `float` | `0.0f` | Corner radius in DIPs. |
| `brush` | `LinearGradientBrush` |  | Stops only; the axis is always vertical. |
| `extent_px` | `float` | `3.0f` | Signed gradient span in device pixels (see above). |
| `stroke_width` | `float` | `1.0f` | Pen width in DIPs. |

## struct StrokeLine

A single straight stroked line segment. The classic raised and sunken bevels (a light edge and a dark edge around a flat fill) are built from these: [draw_bevel_border()](namespace-ui.md#draw_bevel_border) draws four per bevel ring.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `Point` |  | Start point, in DIPs. |
| `to` | `Point` |  | End point, in DIPs. |
| `color` | `Color` |  | The stroke color. |
| `stroke_width` | `float` | `1.0f` | Pen width in DIPs. |

## struct StrokeWavyLine

A wavy line from [`from`](#struct-strokewavyline) to [`to`](#struct-strokewavyline), the underline that marks a [SpellChecker](spell-checker.md)'s misspellings. It is a command of its own, so TestRenderer records one squiggle per word instead of many line segments, and each backend draws its own curve. The wave swings [`amplitude`](#struct-strokewavyline) DIPs to either side of the from→to axis, one full period every [`wavelength`](#struct-strokewavyline) DIPs, starting on the axis.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `Point` |  | Start of the axis, in DIPs. |
| `to` | `Point` |  | End of the axis, in DIPs. |
| `color` | `Color` |  | The stroke color. |
| `stroke_width` | `float` | `1.0f` | Pen width in DIPs. |
| `amplitude` | `float` | `1.0f` | Peak distance from the axis, in DIPs. |
| `wavelength` | `float` | `4.0f` | Length of one full period along the axis, in DIPs. |

## struct StrokePolyline

Straight lines through [`points`](#struct-strokepolyline) in order, with the closing back()-to-front() edge only when [`closed`](#struct-strokepolyline). [TeachingTip](../controls/teaching-tip.md#uiteachingtip)'s tail outlines its two slanted sides this way and leaves open the side it shares with the tip's body.

Example: 
```cpp
const std::vector<ui::Point> tail = {{0, 10}, {8, 0}, {16, 10}};
renderer.fill_polygon(ui::FillPolygon{.points = tail, .fill = ui::colors::White});
renderer.stroke_polyline(ui::StrokePolyline{
    .points       = tail,
    .color        = ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 0, 0, 40),
    .stroke_width = 1.0f,
    .closed       = false, // the two slanted sides only
});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `points` | `std::vector<Point>` |  | Vertices in DIPs, in drawing order. |
| `color` | `Color` |  | [Line](../controls/shapes.md#uiline) color; transparent draws nothing. |
| `stroke_width` | `float` | `1.0f` | [Line](../controls/shapes.md#uiline) width in DIPs; 0 draws nothing. |
| `closed` | `bool` | `false` | Draw the closing back()-to-front() edge too. |

## struct DrawTextRun

Recorded form of [Renderer::draw_text()](renderer.md#draw_text): a UTF-8 string laid out in [`bounds`](#struct-drawtextrun) per [`style`](#struct-drawtextrun).

Example: 
```cpp
// What Renderer::draw_text() draws. In an element of your own:
class Label : public ui::Element
{
    void render_override(ui::Renderer& r, const ui::RenderContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Theme& theme = context.theme;
        r.draw_text("Save", bounds(), theme.colors().text, theme.type.body);
    }
};
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `std::string` |  | The UTF-8 text. |
| `bounds` | `Rect` |  | [Layout](../controls/item-layouts.md#uilayout) box the text is aligned within, in DIPs. |
| `color` | `Color` |  | [Text](../controls/text.md#uitext) color. |
| `style` | `TextStyle` |  | Font, size, weight, alignment and wrapping. |

## struct DrawGeometry

A [PathGeometry](path-geometry.md), filled and then stroked: what every [Shape](../controls/shapes.md#uishape) draws. Either brush may be absent. A gradient's relatively mapped points span [`brush_box`](#struct-drawgeometry) and its absolute ones count from its top-left; a [Shape](../controls/shapes.md#uishape) passes its own layout rect, since a [Shape](../controls/shapes.md#uishape)'s brushes map to the element's top-left. An empty [`brush_box`](#struct-drawgeometry) means the geometry's own bounds.

An [`AcrylicBrush`](acrylic-brush.md) fill depends on drawing order: it blurs whatever was drawn under the geometry before this command, so it must come after the content it sits on. [Window::render()](../tree/window.md#render) draws popups last, so a popup's acrylic blurs the finished tree.

Example: 
```cpp
renderer.draw_geometry(ui::DrawGeometry{
    .geometry     = ui::PathGeometry::ellipse(ui::Point{50, 50}, 40, 40),
    .fill         = ui::Brush{ui::colors::White},
    .stroke       = ui::Brush{ui::Color::from_rgba(0, 120, 215)},
    .stroke_style = {.thickness = 2.0f},
});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `geometry` | `PathGeometry` |  | The figures to paint, in DIPs. |
| `fill` | `std::optional<Brush>` |  | Interior paint; nullopt skips the fill. |
| `stroke` | `std::optional<Brush>` |  | Outline paint; nullopt skips the stroke. |
| `stroke_style` | `StrokeStyle` |  | Pen for [`stroke`](#struct-drawgeometry); ignored when there is none. |
| `brush_box` | `Rect` |  | Box gradients map to; empty uses the geometry's bounds. |

## struct DrawImage

A [Bitmap](bitmap.md) stretched into [`bounds`](#struct-drawimage) per [`stretch`](#struct-drawimage), as drawn by [Image](../controls/image.md#uiimage), [Icon](../controls/icon.md#uiicon) and [PersonPicture](../controls/person-picture.md#uipersonpicture). [Renderer::draw_image()](renderer.md#draw_image) takes the [Bitmap](bitmap.md) itself, while [DrawImageNineSlice](#struct-drawimagenineslice) looks an image up by name. The recorded command keeps [`image_size`](#struct-drawimage) but not the pixels. A backend reads the pixels during the call.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::Bitmap photo = ui::Bitmap::read("avatar.jpg", {.max_width = 96, .max_height = 96});
renderer.draw_image(photo, ui::Rect{0, 0, 48, 48}, ui::Stretch::UniformToFill);
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image_size` | `Size` |  | Source pixel dimensions, for [Stretch](namespace-ui.md#stretch)'s aspect-ratio math. |
| `bounds` | `Rect` |  | Destination rect, in DIPs. |
| `stretch` | `Stretch` | `Stretch::Uniform` | How the image is fitted into [`bounds`](#struct-drawimage). |

## struct DrawImageRect

A [`source`](#struct-drawimagerect) rectangle of a caller-supplied bitmap (in its pixels) drawn into [`bounds`](#struct-drawimagerect), scaled on each axis to fill it. The [Image](../controls/image.md#uiimage) element's stretch modes and nine-grid are built from it: cropping ([Stretch](namespace-ui.md#stretch) None or UniformToFill on a smaller element) is a smaller source rect, and a nine-grid is nine of these. Like [DrawImage](#struct-drawimage), the recorded command keeps the image's size but not its pixels.

Example: 
```cpp
// Draw the top-left 16x16 tile of a sprite sheet at 2x.
const ui::Bitmap sheet = ui::Bitmap::read_png("sprites.png");
renderer.draw_image_rect(sheet, ui::Rect{0, 0, 16, 16}, ui::Rect{0, 0, 32, 32});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image_size` | `Size` |  | Source pixel dimensions. |
| `source` | `Rect` |  | The part of the image drawn, in image pixels. |
| `bounds` | `Rect` |  | Destination rect, in DIPs. |

## struct DrawImageNineSlice

A nine-slice image blit: looks [`image_name`](#struct-drawimagenineslice) up in whatever ImageThemePack the backend was configured with and draws it stretched (corners verbatim, edges stretched along one axis, center stretched along both) to fill [`bounds`](#struct-drawimagenineslice), per [`slice_margins`](#struct-drawimagenineslice). libwinui ships no images itself. Without a matching image, or without a pack, which is the common case, the call draws nothing and is no error, so a control can always ask for image chrome.

Example: 
```cpp
renderer.draw_image_nine_slice("button.normal", ui::Rect{0, 0, 75, 23},
                               ui::Thickness{3});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image_name` | `std::string` |  | [Key](../core/namespace-ui.md#key) into the backend's ImageThemePack. |
| `bounds` | `Rect` |  | Destination rect, in DIPs. |
| `slice_margins` | `Thickness` |  | Corner/edge sizes, in the source image's pixels. |

## struct DrawSvg

An [SvgImage](svg-image.md) drawn into [`bounds`](#struct-drawsvg): its viewport is its natural size (or [`bounds`](#struct-drawsvg)' size when it has none), scaled on each axis to [`bounds`](#struct-drawsvg). The recorded command keeps the natural size, not the markup.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::SvgImage logo = ui::SvgImage::read("logo.svg"); // throws if unreadable
renderer.draw_svg(logo, ui::Rect{0, 0, 64, 64});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `natural_size` | `Size` |  | The document's own size in DIPs; empty when it declares none. |
| `bounds` | `Rect` |  | Destination rect, in DIPs. |

## struct PushClip

Restricts subsequent drawing to [`bounds`](#struct-pushclip) until the matching [PopClip](#struct-popclip). Pushes and pops must balance within a single render() call. A container that clips, such as [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll), pushes before rendering its children and pops right after.

Example: 
```cpp
void render_visible(ui::Renderer& renderer, const ui::RenderContext& context, const ui::Rect& viewport,
                    const std::vector<ui::Element*>& visible_children)
{
    renderer.push_clip(viewport);
    for (const ui::Element* child : visible_children)
    {
        child->render(renderer, context);
    }
    renderer.pop_clip();
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bounds` | `Rect` |  | The clip rect, in DIPs (transformed by any enclosing [PushTransform](#struct-pushtransform)). |

## struct PushClipEllipse

An elliptical clip, such as [PersonPicture](../controls/person-picture.md#uipersonpicture)'s circular photo mask. It ends with the same [PopClip](#struct-popclip) as a rect clip. A backend that pops each kind of clip differently tracks which kind it pushed.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::Bitmap photo = ui::Bitmap::read("avatar.jpg");
renderer.push_clip_ellipse(ui::Point{24, 24}, 24, 24);
renderer.draw_image(photo, ui::Rect{0, 0, 48, 48}, ui::Stretch::UniformToFill);
renderer.pop_clip();
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `center` | `Point` |  | Center of the ellipse, in DIPs. |
| `radius_x` | `float` | `0.0f` | Horizontal radius, in DIPs. |
| `radius_y` | `float` | `0.0f` | Vertical radius, in DIPs. |

## struct PopClip

Ends the innermost [PushClip](#struct-pushclip), [PushClipEllipse](#struct-pushclipellipse) or [PushClipRoundedRect](push-clip-rounded-rect.md).

## struct PushTransform

An affine transform of everything drawn until the matching [PopTransform](#struct-poptransform): a point `p` lands at `(p.x * scale + p.y * m21 + offset.x, p.x * m12 + p.y * scale_y + offset.y)` (a [`Matrix`](matrix.md) in render/PathGeometry.hpp's row-vector convention), and nested pushes compose (the inner one applies first). [Scroll](../layout/scroll.md#uiscroll) zooms this way: its content is laid out once at its natural size and drawn magnified. [`scale_y`](#scale_y) differs from [`scale`](#scale) for [ScaleToFit](../layout/scale-to-fit.md#uiscaletofit)'s `Stretch::Fill`. [`m12`](#m12) and [`m21`](#m21) are non-zero only for a rotation, which comes from [Element::set_rotation()](../tree/element.md#set_rotation). Clips pushed inside a transform are transformed with it, and a rotated clip becomes its bounding box. Pushes and pops balance within one render() call.

Example: 
```cpp
void render_zoomed(ui::Renderer& renderer, const ui::RenderContext& context, const ui::Element& content)
{
    renderer.push_transform(2.0f, ui::Point{10, 10}); // uniform 2x zoom, then offset
    content.render(renderer, context);
    renderer.pop_transform();
}
```

### scale

```cpp
float scale = 1.0f
```

Horizontal scale ([Matrix::m11](matrix.md#m11)); also the vertical one when uniform.

### offset

```cpp
Point offset {}
```

Translation applied after scaling, in DIPs.

### scale_y

```cpp
float scale_y = 1.0f
```

Vertical scale ([Matrix::m22](matrix.md#m22)).

### m12

```cpp
float m12 = 0.0f
```

Rotation/skew term; 0 unless the element is rotated.

### m21

```cpp
float m21 = 0.0f
```

Rotation/skew term; 0 unless the element is rotated.

### matrix

```cpp
Matrix matrix() const
```

The same transform as a [Matrix](matrix.md).

## struct PopTransform

Ends the innermost [PushTransform](#struct-pushtransform).

## struct PushOpacityLayer

Draws every call between this and the matching [PopOpacityLayer](#struct-popopacitylayer) as one layer at [`opacity`](#struct-pushopacitylayer). Flyouts and dialogs fade in and out this way: [Window::render()](../tree/window.md#render) wraps a flyout's popup, or a dialog's scrim and content together, in one layer at [Element::transition_opacity()](../tree/element.md#transition_opacity).

At [`opacity`](#struct-pushopacitylayer) 1, which is every [Element](../tree/element.md) that isn't fading, the layer must look like no layer, and a backend may skip it. At 0 or below a backend need not draw the contents at all. Pushes and pops must balance within a single render() call, like [PushClip](#struct-pushclip) and [PopClip](#struct-popclip), and the two kinds nest inside each other freely.

Example: 
```cpp
void render_faded(ui::Renderer& renderer, const ui::RenderContext& context, const ui::Element& popup_content)
{
    renderer.push_opacity_layer(0.5f);
    popup_content.render(renderer, context); // drawn at half opacity, as one layer
    renderer.pop_opacity_layer();
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opacity` | `float` | `1.0f` | Layer opacity, 0..1; 1 is a no-op. |

## struct PopOpacityLayer

Ends the innermost [PushOpacityLayer](#struct-pushopacitylayer).

## struct SetRasterization

The rasterization policy for the whole frame. [Window::render()](../tree/window.md#render) emits it once, at the start, from [Theme::rasterization](../themes/theme.md#rasterization). Because it is a command, TestRenderer records it and [describe()](namespace-ui.md#describe) prints it, so a test can check that a theme asks for aliased rendering without comparing pixels. The backend applies [`snap_to_device_pixels`](#struct-setrasterization) while drawing, by rounding each primitive's coordinates to the nearest device pixel, so it stays correct under DPI scaling. [Layout](../controls/item-layouts.md#uilayout) is unaffected and stays resolution-independent.

Example: 
```cpp
// A renderer of your own receives it first in every frame and keeps it for what follows.
class ExportRenderer : public ui::Renderer
{
public:
    void set_rasterization(const ui::SetRasterization& policy) override
    {
        antialias_shapes_ = policy.geometry == ui::GeometryAA::Antialiased;
        text_smoothing_   = policy.text;
        snap_to_pixels_   = policy.snap_to_device_pixels;
    }

private:
    bool       antialias_shapes_ = true;
    ui::TextAA text_smoothing_   = ui::TextAA::Grayscale;
    bool       snap_to_pixels_   = false;
};
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `geometry` | `GeometryAA` | `GeometryAA::Antialiased` | Edge policy for shapes and lines. |
| `text` | `TextAA` | `TextAA::Grayscale` | [Text](../controls/text.md#uitext) smoothing policy. |
| `snap_to_device_pixels` | `bool` | `false` | Round primitives to device pixels. |
